Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (performance gains, cluster consistency), pain points (multivalued field nulls, SOAR overspilling, redundant SUM reuse), and acceptance criteria (edge case handling, measurement metrics, validation requirements) for the Elasticsearch query planner SUM(X+a) optimization requirement.

End-user perspective identifies two primary concerns: (1) query optimization for SUM(X+a) aggregations to reduce computational overhead in analytics workloads, with expectation of automatic rewriting to SUM(X) + a*COUNT(X) form, and (2) cluster stability under SOAR spillover requiring consistent node behavior. Critical technical blocker: multivalued field semantics require null-safety guarantees before optimization can be safely applied.

End-user requirements focus on optimizing SUM(X+a) query patterns to reduce computational overhead and enable result reuse, while maintaining consistent cluster performance during SOAR overflow. Key challenge: handling multivalued fields where X+a becomes null, requiring conditional optimization logic. Business value: reduced query latency and improved resource utilization in large-scale aggregation scenarios.

End user requires query optimization for SUM(X+a) rewrites with correct multivalued field semantics, combined with consistent cluster behavior under SOAR spillover to enable predictable performance at scale.

The requirement set conflates two distinct concerns (query optimization and cluster resource consistency) with unresolved technical ambiguities around multi-valued field handling, NULL semantics, and distributed result reuse. Chain-of-Thought analysis reveals: (1) the SUM(X+a) optimization assumes single-valued X but the codebase supports multi-valued fields—requiring explicit NULL handling rules; (2) SOAR spillover impact on 'consistency' is undefined (memory vs. coordination); (3) result reuse in distributed settings needs cache coherency specification.

Five clarification questions raised to resolve ambiguities in the SUM(X+a) query optimization requirement: (1) multivalued field handling strategy, (2) constant operand scope, (3) relationship to cluster consistency concern, (4) NULL-counting semantics, and (5) per-value vs. per-document contribution logic for multivalued fields.

Five critical clarification questions identified addressing: (1) NULL semantics contradiction in multivalued field handling, (2) constant operand scope (literals vs. expressions), (3) independence vs. interaction between cluster consistency and query optimization requirements, (4) execution model for multi-valued fields under optimization, and (5) NULL propagation rules. These ambiguities must be resolved before implementation to ensure mathematical correctness and operational consistency.

Refined two primary requirements: (1) SUM(X+a) optimization scoped to numeric literals only with explicit NULL handling for multivalued fields (disabled by default for safety); (2) Cluster consistency under SOAR overflow confirmed as independent from query optimization but operationally coupled. Pending clarification on result reuse caching scope and multivalued field opt-in mechanism.

EndUser confirms SUM(X+a) optimization scope (numeric literals only) and refines multivalued field semantics to treat each value independently with explicit NULL handling. Both optimization and cluster consistency requirements are validated as independent concerns with no mutual blocking dependencies.

End-user requirements validated and refined: SUM(X+a) optimization confirmed for numeric literals only with explicit multivalued field NULL semantics; query planner optimization and cluster consistency confirmed as independent operational concerns; optimization validity unaffected by SOAR spillover but spillover may impact execution latency.

Consolidated 5 structured elicitation records from elasticsearch_2026q1 case addressing: (1) SUM(X+a) query optimizer rewrite rule with numeric-literal-only scope; (2) multivalued field NULL semantics and independent value contribution; (3) cluster size consistency under SOAR spillover as independent operational concern; (4) scope boundary confirmation; (5) performance mitigation guidance. All records validated against end-user confirmations and refined through iterative Socratic questioning. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability applied; MoSCoW prioritization assigned.
